chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurrat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to David (peace be upon him): 'You are an excellent servant, if only you did not eat from the public treasury (bayt al-mal) and did not work with your own hand.' He said: 'So David (peace be upon him) wept for forty mornings. Then God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to iron to become pliable for His servant David, so God Almighty made the iron pliable for him. He would make a coat of mail every day and sell it for one thousand dirhams. He made three hundred and sixty coats of mail and sold them for three hundred and sixty thousand, and he became independent of the public treasury.'
ai.seo_question: How did Prophet David earn his livelihood independently according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* under the chapter of trade, this hadith illustrates the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Prophet David’s transition from reliance on the public treasury (*bayt al-mal*) to self-sufficiency through manual labor. The narrative highlights the virtue of earning one's livelihood honestly, using the divine gift of iron pliability to produce three hundred and sixty armor pieces, thereby establishing a model of economic independence for the community.
